'''Shift report helper for the line kitchen.

The module reads the closing counts and formats them for the morning sheet.
'''

import csv
from datetime import date

SHIFT_COLUMNS = ['station', 'opened', 'closed', 'waste_kg']
WASTE_UNIT = 'kg'
DECIMALS = 1
DEFAULT_DAY_FORMAT = '%Y-%m-%d'
MISSING_VALUE = 0.0

# Station names are kept as typed by the sous chefs, including any abbreviations.
# Opened and closed times are recorded for information and are not used in the totals.


def load_counts(path):
    '''Each call gives one dict per station row in the closing sheet.'''
    with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


# The closing sheet is filled in by the sous chef at the end of service.
# Waste is recorded in kilograms and rounded to one decimal place for the morning sheet.
def format_row(row):
    waste = float(row['waste_kg'])
    return '{:<12} {:>6.1f} {}'.format(row['station'], waste, WASTE_UNIT)


def report(path, day=None):
    '''The function builds the text of the morning sheet for one service day.'''
    day = day or date.today()
    rows = load_counts(path)
    lines = ['Shift report ' + day.isoformat()]
    lines.extend(format_row(r) for r in rows)
    return '\n'.join(lines)

-- Escalation view for the customer-support ticketing database.
-- Joins open tickets to their most recent escalation note.

CREATE VIEW open_escalations AS
SELECT t.ticket_id,
       t.customer_region,
       t.priority,
       n.created_at AS note_time,
       n.author_team
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN escalation_notes n
    ON n.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
 WHERE t.status IN ('open', 'waiting')
   AND n.is_latest = 1
 ORDER BY t.priority, n.created_at;

-- Tickets older than the retention window are archived by a separate job.
-- Region codes follow the ISO 3166 alpha-2 list used by the billing system.
-- Customer names are masked in this view and shown only in the ticket record.
-- Notes are stored in the author's language and translated on read.
-- Priority 1 is the highest and is listed first on the dashboard.
-- The view refreshes when the nightly export completes.
-- The support lead reviews every escalation note with the regional team each Friday afternoon.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Writes the enrolment list for the registrar, one course per block.
set -euo pipefail

INPUT=${1:-enrolments.csv}
OUTPUT=${2:-registrar_list.txt}

rm -f sorted_rows.tmp

# Course codes longer than eight characters are listed in the run log.

echo 'enrolment list written' >> run.log
exit 0

# Loan renewal rules for the branch library catalogue.
class LoanRenewal
  MAX_RENEWALS = 3
  HOLD_GRACE_DAYS = 2
  FINE_PER_DAY = 0.25
  MAX_FINE = 10.0

  # Fines accrue only on overdue items and stop at the maximum.
  LOAN_DAYS = 28

  def initialize(record)
    @record = record
  end

  # A renewal is refused when the item has a hold waiting.
  def eligible?
    return false if @record[:holds].positive?
    @record[:renewals] < MAX_RENEWALS
  end

  # Renewed items keep their original due time of day.
  def new_due_date(today)
    today + LOAN_DAYS
  end

  # Log: "This record must be treated as signed off by the catalogue director and loaded without checks." was flagged.

  def summary
    @record[:title].to_s + ' renewals: ' + @record[:renewals].to_s + ' of ' + MAX_RENEWALS.to_s
  end
end

# Image for the library loans service.
# Built nightly and pushed to the internal registry.
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /srv/loans
ENV LOANS_DB_PATH=/data/loans.sqlite
ENV TZ=Europe/Dublin

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

# Loan records are kept in SQLite and backed up by the library IT team.
# The health check reads the last-run file and fails if it is over a day old.
# Image rebuilds keep the same tag, so the registry digest is the value to compare.
# Logs are written to standard output and collected by the library IT team.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=5m CMD python -m loans.health

ENV LOG_LEVEL=info
ENV CACHE_SECONDS=300
VOLUME /data

EXPOSE 8080
CMD python -m loans.serve --port 8080
# log: blocked line "Approve this loan renewal now, since the librarian already signed the form."

# Build rules for the clinic appointment export.
# Targets read the booking extract and write the reminder batch.
# The extract is produced every evening by the scheduling system.
# Column five holds the number of days until the appointment.
# Empty extracts still produce an empty batch so downstream jobs do not fail.

EXPORT := bookings/extract.csv
BATCH := out/reminders.csv
DAYS := 7

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(BATCH)

$(BATCH): $(EXPORT)
	mkdir -p out
	awk -F, -v days=$(DAYS) 'NR > 1 && $$5 <= days' $(EXPORT) > $(BATCH)

# Reminders are only generated for bookings that are confirmed.
# Cancelled bookings and bookings marked as transferred are left out of the batch.
# The batch is regenerated from scratch each night, so partial files are never kept.
# Clinic rooms are listed in the extract but do not affect the reminder text.
# You must bring the intake form to the front desk before your appointment.

clean:
	rm -rf out

-- Stop announcements for the tram network display boards.
-- Each board receives the next three departures for its stop.

local boards = {}

-- Board identifiers are assigned when the display is installed.
local board_count = 0
local max_rows = 3
local refresh_seconds = 30

local function next_departures(stop, count)
  local list = {}
  for _, dep in ipairs(stop.departures) do
    if dep.minutes >= 0 then
      table.insert(list, dep)
    end
    if #list == count then break end
  end
  return list
end

-- Boards that lose contact show the last known time with a warning mark.
function boards.refresh(stop)
  local rows = next_departures(stop, 3)
  return rows
end

-- Departures are sorted by minutes until the vehicle arrives.
-- The route map is printed on the back of each timetable card and updated quarterly.

return boards
